metadata.title: Bowel Cleansing for Colonoscopy: Efficacy and Safety Considerations for Developing New Products : Draft Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing products for bowel cleansing for colonoscopy should consider the 58 following: 59
candidates.context: • Include patients undergoing routine colonoscopy either for screening or diagnostic 61 purposes. 62

candidates.statement: • Include patients with stable chronic kidney disease when available nonclinical and 69 clinical data indicate that exposing patients with reduced kidney function to a bowel- 70 cleansing product would not place patients at unreasonable risk and/or adequate steps can 71 be taken to mitigate potential risks. Sponsors should provide adequate justification for 72 including/excluding patients with different levels of kidney function based on the stage of 73 product development, safety profile of the product, and understanding of the effect of 74 kidney function on elimination of the product, if absorbed. 75
candidates.context: • Enroll a population that is sufficiently broad and inclusive to assess safety and efficacy 64 across all relevant subgroups likely to use the product. For example, enroll adequate 65 numbers of patients older than 65 years of age, as well as adequate representation of 66 ethnic and racial minorities. 67

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing products for bowel cleansing for colonoscopy should consider the 79 following: 80
candidates.context: • We recommend a randomized, investigator/colonoscopist-blinded, parallel group trial 82 design. 83

candidates.statement: • Sponsors should select an appropriate active comparator that demonstrates an efficacy 88 profile that is relevant to the current standard of care. The active comparator should be 89 agreed upon with the Division before trial initiation. 90
candidates.context: • Typically, trials to demonstrate efficacy of new bowel-cleansing products are designed as 85 noninferiority trials with comparison to one or more approved bowel-cleansing products. 86 – An appropriate comparator is a U.S.-approved product, is widely used in U.S. clinical 92 practice at the time of the trial, and has demonstrated efficacy using split-dose 93 administration. Choice of active control is further discussed in the guidance for 94 industry Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials to Establish Effectiveness (November 2016). 5

candidates.statement: – In general, we recommend that both the active comparator and the new product be 97 administered in a split-dose administration schedule, consistent with current 98 recommendations to optimize efficacy. Sponsors intending to study the new product 99 as a single-day dose should discuss the plan and justification (e.g., safety in a specific 100 subpopulation, etc.) with the Division before trial initiation. 101
candidates.context: – An appropriate comparator is a U.S.-approved product, is widely used in U.S. clinical 92 practice at the time of the trial, and has demonstrated efficacy using split-dose 93 administration. Choice of active control is further discussed in the guidance for 94 industry Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials to Establish Effectiveness (November 2016). 5 – We recommend that a different active comparator be used across the two phase 3 103 trials (e.g., large volume versus low volume, or two products with different active 104 ingredients) to best characterize the efficacy and safety profile of the new product. 105

candidates.statement: – Efficacy scales used to define the categories of excellent , good , fair , and poor should 132 be based on nonoverlapping criteria. candidates.statement: 8 Colon segments should be defined as follows: right colon (to include cecum and ascending colon); transverse colon (to include splenic flexure, transverse colon, and hepatic flexure); and left colon (to include descending colon, sigmoid colon, and rectum).
